article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Permanent Marker × Zoap
Breeder: LIT Farms
THC Content: 23–29%
CBD Content: Low to trace, generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , caryophyllene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Blueberry candy, sweet citrus, floral soap
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Blue Sharpie belongs to a newer class of marijuana strains whose aromas seem almost impossible until the flower is actually opened. Sweet blue fruit and candy sit beside something much stranger: ink, fresh rubber, chemical solvent, floral soap, and gasoline. The cultivar most consistently associated with the Blue Sharpie or Blue Sharpies name is LIT Farms’ Sharpiez, an indica-leaning hybrid made from Permanent Marker × Zoap. LIT Farms officially confirms that parentage and describes the flower as combining pungent gas and ink-like funk with a sweeter, soapy middle and earthy finish.

Cultivated examples sold as Blue Sharpies have carried the same Permanent Marker × Zoap lineage, including flower from Alternative Solutions in Washington, D.C. With THC commonly reaching the mid-to-upper 20% range and an effect that moves from energetic euphoria toward substantial body relaxation, this weed offers considerably more than unusual branding. Its appeal comes from contrast: dark resinous buds, bright fruit sweetness, aggressive chemical terpenes, and a high that can feel lively at first before becoming noticeably heavier.
Genetics and Lineage

The best-documented genetic foundation for Blue Sharpie is Permanent Marker × Zoap. LIT Farms releases this cross under the name Sharpiez, and its own current strain profile confirms the pairing. Other licensed cultivators have marketed the same genetics as Blue Sharpies, making the names closely linked even though Sharpiez is the breeder’s formal designation. That distinction is useful because “Blue Sharpie” has occasionally been applied to unrelated or poorly documented flower. For an authority strain profile, the LIT Farms Permanent Marker × Zoap version provides the strongest traceable pedigree.

Permanent Marker contributes the darker, more aggressive half of the cross. Its family tree combines Biscotti , Jealousy , and Sherb-related genetics, creating the powerful chemical-marker aroma that made the cultivar famous. Zoap softens those characteristics through a distinctly sweeter combination of fruit, flowers, candy, and perfumed soap. Bringing the two together produces marijuana that can smell simultaneously artificial and natural: berry syrup beside petroleum, citrus peel beside marker ink, and floral sweetness wrapped around pungent gas.

The pairing also explains the appearance of many Blue Sharpie phenotypes. Both parents are known for dense contemporary flower architecture, considerable trichome coverage, and the ability to develop dark coloration late in bloom. Blue Sharpies grown commercially have displayed deep purple flowers with blue accents underneath heavy frost, giving the “Blue” portion of the name a visual connection in addition to the berry-like flavor.
Effects and Experience

Blue Sharpie generally announces itself above the shoulders first. The initial phase can produce a rapid increase in mood, mental engagement, and sociability, with conversation and creative activities becoming more entertaining. LIT Farms describes Sharpiez as having a fast, intense cerebral onset accompanied by creativity and pronounced euphoria. That energetic beginning can make the cultivar seem more balanced than its indica-leaning classification would suggest, particularly when consumed in a modest amount.

Physical relaxation develops more steadily. Instead of abruptly replacing the head high, it builds underneath it until the body feels noticeably calmer and heavier. A comfortable chair, music, movies, gaming, or casual socializing may become increasingly appealing as the session moves forward. Larger servings tend to emphasize this second stage considerably more, potentially turning an initially playful experience into deep decompression and reduced motivation.

Potency is worth respecting. Alternative Solutions flower sold as Blue Sharpies has tested at approximately 22.86% THC, while verified Sharpiez clone material is commonly listed around 26–29%. Consumers therefore should not assume every batch will have identical strength. High doses can cause dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, short-term memory disruption, or anxiety, particularly in people sensitive to intense THC effects.
Medical Benefits

The transition from brighter cerebral effects into physical calm may appeal to medical marijuana consumers seeking a hybrid that does not immediately produce heavy sedation. Some patients choose cannabis with this type of profile when temporary stress, appetite reduction, muscular tension, low mood, or physical discomfort makes relaxing difficult. Moderate servings may preserve enough mental engagement for afternoon or early-evening use, while stronger doses can shift the experience toward a more restful state.

Terpene composition provides useful context. Commercial Blue Sharpies flower has been associated with beta-caryophyllene, limonene, and humulene, while other Sharpiez releases identify limonene, caryophyllene, and linalool as major aromatic compounds. These terpenes help explain the cultivar’s mixture of citrus brightness, peppery spice, flowers, earth, and fuel. Individual batches can vary considerably, however, so the laboratory report attached to a specific product is more informative than a universal strain profile.

Blue Sharpie itself has not been clinically established as a treatment for anxiety, depression, insomnia, chronic pain, or another medical condition. People using cannabis medically should consider THC concentration, terpene testing, personal tolerance, medications, and the advice of an appropriate healthcare professional rather than relying on strain names alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Few cultivars make the name feel as literal as Blue Sharpie. The first smell from a properly cured jar can suggest permanent-marker ink or solvent before sweeter notes have time to emerge. Blueberry-like fruit, blue raspberry candy, tart citrus, and floral soap gradually appear beneath that chemical edge. When the flower is broken apart, skunky gas and pepper can become considerably stronger, producing an aroma that resembles berry candy opened near fresh paint or rubber.

The palate is more approachable than the aroma. Sweet fruit often leads the inhale, with berry and citrus providing an almost candy-like opening. Zoap contributes floral and perfumed qualities through the middle, while Permanent Marker becomes increasingly noticeable toward the finish. Gasoline, earthy spice, pepper, and the distinctive marker-like character can remain on the tongue after exhalation. LIT Farms describes the underlying Sharpiez cross as moving from pungent gas and ink into sweetness, soap, and warm earth.

That tension gives the strain an advantage over more straightforward fruit-flavored weed. Without Permanent Marker, the profile could become overly sweet and perfumed; without Zoap, the chemical gas might feel one-dimensional. Blue Sharpie works because neither side completely wins.
Growing Information

LIT Farms’ Sharpiez is a feminized photoperiod cultivar with an indoor flowering period of approximately eight to nine weeks. Independent seed listings carrying the official LIT Farms release specify 56–63 days and describe the plant as medium in height and suitable for both indoor and outdoor cultivation. Verified clone material similarly lists an eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle and high yield potential.

Indoors, the hybrid benefits from establishing a broad canopy before flowering. Topping and gentle low-stress training can help distribute branches beneath the available lighting, while removing weak lower growth allows the plant to devote more energy to productive tops. Stretch is generally manageable compared with highly sativa-dominant cannabis, but adequate spacing remains important as the flower sites begin stacking. Mature buds can become dense and heavily coated in resin, so airflow should reach both the exterior and interior of the canopy.

Humidity management becomes particularly important during the last several weeks. Tight flowers can retain moisture, increasing mold risk when air remains stagnant. Outdoors, a late-September to early-October harvest is a reasonable target in climates capable of supporting an eight-to-nine-week bloom cycle, although actual readiness should always be determined by flower and trichome maturity. Careful post-harvest handling is equally valuable. Excessive heat or rapid drying can eliminate the berry, citrus, and floral top notes, leaving behind a much simpler earthy-gas profile rather than the layered character Blue Sharpie is supposed to deliver.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Blue Sharpie?

The best-documented Blue Sharpie genetics are Permanent Marker × Zoap. LIT Farms officially breeds this cross as Sharpiez, while licensed cultivators and retailers have also used the Blue Sharpie or Blue Sharpies name for the same genetic pairing.
Who bred Blue Sharpie?
LIT Farms is the documented breeder of the Permanent Marker × Zoap cultivar officially called Sharpiez. Blue Sharpie and Blue Sharpies are market names commonly associated with this genetic line.
Is Blue Sharpie indica or sativa?
It is generally considered an indica-leaning hybrid. The experience can initially feel cerebral, euphoric, and creative before gradually developing a stronger relaxing body component.
How strong is Blue Sharpie?

Potency varies by grower and phenotype. Commercial Blue Sharpies flower has tested around 22.86% THC, while Sharpiez clone material commonly lists approximately 26–29% THC. High-potency batches are better suited to consumers who already understand their tolerance.
What does Blue Sharpie taste like?

Expect blue-fruit or berry candy mixed with citrus, floral soap, chemical marker funk, diesel, earth, and pepper. Sweeter Zoap characteristics tend to appear early, while the Permanent Marker side becomes more obvious through the gassy, solvent-like finish.
Final Thoughts on Blue Sharpie

Blue Sharpie succeeds because it brings together two strains with unusually recognizable personalities. Permanent Marker supplies chemical ink, gas, earth, and potency, while Zoap introduces sweeter fruit, flowers, and soap-like perfume. LIT Farms’ Permanent Marker × Zoap cross officially appears as Sharpiez, while Blue Sharpie or Blue Sharpies has become a common alternative label for commercially cultivated expressions of the same genetics.

Beyond the unusual aroma, the cultivar offers the characteristics expected from premium contemporary cannabis: dense dark flowers, substantial resin, high THC potential, and an effect that changes noticeably over time. Cerebral euphoria and creativity dominate the beginning before a deeper body calm starts taking control. For marijuana consumers who enjoy berry sweetness but want something considerably stranger and more pungent than conventional fruit-flavored weed, Blue Sharpie provides a distinctive mixture of candy, flowers, ink, rubber, and fuel that is difficult to confuse with almost anything else.
